title: The Deer Park
hookLine: the five agree to ignore him, then rise to greet him as he comes

lines: FIVE OLD FRIENDS IN A GROVE.
cards: Arms folded. Nobody gets up. Five men are sitting in a grove outside the city of Benares, and that is their plan.
They are the five companions who starved themselves beside Siddhartha. When he began eating again and gave up the starving, they walked out on him in disgust. He's gone soft, they said.
Now, weeks after that night under the tree, they see a figure coming down the path. It's him. They agree: we won't stand.
We won't take his bowl. Maybe we'll leave a seat out, if he wants it. And then he gets closer.

teach.b: The old texts tell it with a smile. As he comes near, the plan simply falls apart. One of them gets up and takes his bowl and robe.
Another sets out a seat. Another brings water to wash his feet. Nobody decides to do it.
The place is called Isipatana, the Deer Park, near Benares; in Pali, a migadaya, a deer park. Today it's Sarnath, and pilgrims still walk there. But the five aren't won over yet.
They greet him as you'd greet an equal, calling him friend and using his family name. He tells them not to. I've found what I was looking for, he says.
Listen, and you can find it too. They push back. You couldn't find it when you were starving yourself, they say; how could you find it now that you've gone back to eating?
Three times he makes his claim, and three times they refuse it.

teach.h: HAVE I EVER SPOKEN LIKE THIS?
teach.b: Then he asks one quiet question: have you ever heard me speak like this before?
And they have to admit they haven't. All that time side by side, and he had never said he'd arrived. So they settle down, and they listen.
The story is honest about all of it. The five aren't fools; their doubt is fair. And they get up anyway, before their minds have caught up with their feet.
Something in the way he walked told them more than their plan did. Standing up didn't mean they agreed. It meant they were willing to hear him.

how: Buddhist pilgrims travel to Sarnath, the old Deer Park near Varanasi, to remember where the Buddha first taught.

o: the Deer Park near Benares, today's Sarnath
a hermit's cave in the Himalayan foothills
the royal garden where Siddhartha grew up

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: the question that made them listen

s: the five welcomed him because they already agreed with him
they stood up before they agreed. three times they refused his claim.
the Deer Park is today's Sarnath, near Varanasi
the five had left him because he started eating again
they thought he had given up the struggle.

games.q: you're one of the five. you've all agreed not to stand for him. he's walking up the path. what happens?
o: you keep your seat, like you agreed.
you get up and take his bowl.
games.why: the plan falls apart as he comes near: one takes his bowl and robe, one sets a seat, one brings water for his feet.

practice: The five were on their feet before their minds had caught up; watch for that in your own body now. An itch, and the hand is already moving; a sound, and the head has already turned.
Each time, just notice which moved first, the body or the plan, and come back to the breath; no need to stop it.

wordCard.voice: Isipatana. The deer park near Benares, today's Sarnath: the grove where the five stood up, and where the Buddha first taught.

orig.note: Pali: a deer park. Isipatana migadaya, the Deer Park near Benares.

carryVoice: Your line: they stood up. Tomorrow, the Deer Park hears its first teaching.
